sentiment.rationale: The document shows strong operational momentum (record ad sales, record TV time share, 17% revenue growth) but the headline EPS miss due to a one-time Brazil tax charge and the absence of any formal 2026 guidance (deferred to January) leave forward expectations unchanged. Management's confident language ('feeling good about our growth trajectory') is not backed by a guidance raise, and the structural risk of the Brazil tax continuing (though small) and the lack of concrete 2026 numbers keep the score neutral.

summary.eps: $5.87 versus roughly $6.96 consensus, an optical miss attributable to the Brazil charge.
summary.guidance: No full-year 2026 guidance given, deferred to the January call. No 2026 advertising revenue guidance provided.
summary.margin: Operating margin 28%, down from 30% a year earlier and below the 31.5% guidance, driven by a $619M Brazil tax expense.
key_risks: The EPS/margin miss itself, even if one-time.
The Brazil Supreme Court ruled against Netflix 7–4 on the tax scope.
No 2026 numbers on the table yet, with the market asked to wait until January.
Intensifying live-sports competition (Apple F1, Paramount UFC).
WBD / Warner Bros. acquisition rumours in the background (regulatory and execution overhang).
key_opportunities: Record share of TV time in Q3: 8.6% in the U.S. and 9.4% in the U.K.
Best ad-sales quarter ever, on track to more than double ad revenue in 2025.
Canelo-Crawford fight drew 41M+ live viewers and ranked top 10 in 91 countries.
Approaching 1 billion people globally for programming, still only ~7% of addressable consumer-spend market and ~10% of TV time in biggest markets.
